stories.headline: The United States put 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed
stories.body:
The United States put 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods on Saturday [c2]. US President Donald Trump first announced the 50% tariffs on July 20 [c12]. Trump said the reason was Canadian bans on the sale of US alcohol in provincial stores [c12].

The tariffs affect about $20 billion of Canadian imports [c7]. This amount represents about 5% of total Canadian exports [c7]. Canadian exports to the US totaled $409 billion last year [c11]. Those exports accounted for 73 percent of all Canadian exports [c11]. Canadian Federation of Independent Business president Dan Kelly gave an estimate about the impact [c4]. Kelly estimated that 40% of small Canadian exporters will be directly hit by the US tariffs [c4].

Trade talks between the two countries collapsed [c1]. After the talks collapsed, Trump wrote a message on social media [c1]. Trump wrote that Canada wants the benefits of being a US state without being one [c1]. Trump also spoke on Fox News [c6]. Trump said Canadians were foolish to engage in a trade war with the US [c6]. He said Canadians are foolish to think they will win [c6].

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer spoke on Saturday [c8]. Greer said there are no plans to resume trade talks with Canada [c8]. Canada and Mexico formally requested a 16-year renewal of the USMCA trade pact this summer [c5]. But Trump refused to renew the USMCA trade agreement [c5].

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pledged to respond to the US tariffs [c3]. Carney promised to match US tariffs dollar for dollar starting September 8 [c3]. The Canadian tariffs will cover items including steel, dairy, appliances, and electronics [c3].

Carney said US negotiators made threats during trade talks [c9]. Carney said they made threats against the French language, Quebec culture, and Canadian culture [c9]. Carney also visited China in January [c10]. During that visit, Carney agreed to reduce tariffs on a capped number of Chinese electric vehicles [c10]. In exchange, China lowered its duties on Canadian canola [c10].

stories.headline: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned against holding national elections during the war
stories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that holding elections during the war is a huge risk [c13]. Zelenskyy said elections would be a tsunami for the state that will split Ukraine [c13]. Ukraine suspended national elections under martial law after Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 [c14]. Zelenskyy's five-year presidential term formally expired in May 2024 [c14].

Ousted former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov publicly called for Ukraine to organize fresh elections despite the ongoing war [c15]. Fedorov spoke in a BBC interview [c17]. Fedorov said Zelenskyy should face questions regarding his awareness of potential inner-circle corruption [c17]. His comment came after a money laundering investigation [c17]. Ukraine's anti-corruption bureau uncovered a scheme misappropriating more than $3 million in Ukrainian currency [c18]. The money was used to pay bail for a former energy minister accused of money laundering [c18].

Zelenskyy also discussed military concerns [c16]. Zelenskyy said Russia has a stockpile of between 600 and 630 high-speed ballistic missiles [c16]. He said Russia seeks to produce over 100 a month [c16]. Zelenskyy said he believes Russia will try to conscript an additional 300,000 soldiers after its parliamentary elections in September [c20].

Foreign allies announced plans to send aid to Ukraine [c19, c21]. Germany agreed to supply Ukraine with about 600 PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors in 2027 and 2028 [c19]. Norway announced plans to give 85 billion Norwegian crowns in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year [c21]. That support equals $9.2 billion [c21].

stories.headline: Iran announced a major natural gas discovery in Fars province containing recoverable energy reserves
stories.body:
Iran announced the discovery of more than 200 billion cubic metres of natural gas in Fars province [c22]. Officials said over 160 billion cubic metres of the gas is potentially recoverable [c22]. Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad spoke about the discovery [c23]. Paknejad said the discovery contains more than 7.5 trillion cubic feet of gas [c23]. He said around 5.7 trillion cubic feet of that gas is recoverable [c23]. Paknejad described the newly discovered gas as sweet [c27]. He said low levels of hydrogen sulphide will lower development and operating costs [c27].

The discovery comes after damage to Iranian energy facilities [c24]. Attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure started in late February [c24]. The attacks reduced Iran's daily gas production capacity by around a quarter [c24]. Iran's pre-war natural gas production was estimated at about 650 million cubic metres per day [c28].

Political tensions remain high in the region [c25, c26]. US President Donald Trump shared a graphic on Truth Social [c25]. The graphic depicted the Strait of Hormuz as new US territory [c25]. Iranian Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei issued a warning to nearby countries [c26]. Rezaei warned neighboring countries that Iran will consider them enemies if they join the US economic war [c26].

stories.headline: Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks in Bay of Bengal off Odisha coast triggering rescue operation
stories.body:
A Panama-flagged bulk carrier named M.V. Ocean Winner sank in the Bay of Bengal off the coast of Odisha [c29]. M.V. Ocean Winner sank about 230 to 240 nautical miles off the coast [c39]. The ship was carrying 72,100 metric tonnes of iron ore [c39]. The vessel departed Paradip Port late on August 20, 2026 [c31]. Specifically, the ship departed the Paradip coast at 10:42 pm on August 20 [c40]. The vessel was carrying iron ore fines [c40].

Initial reports from Indian maritime authorities said M.V. Ocean Winner was bound for China [c41]. But other government information indicated Singapore as its destination [c41]. Communication with M.V. Ocean Winner was lost 36 hours after its departure [c32]. The loss of communication prompted a search and rescue request to the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre [c32]. Victory Star Group Co Ltd requested search and rescue assistance after communication was lost late on August 22 [c43].

The Andaman & Nicobar Command reported that M.V. Ocean Winner sent a distress alert on Saturday [c42]. The alert came from a position around 300 nautical miles north-northwest of Diglipur [c42]. M.V. Ocean Winner had 24 crew members onboard [c30]. The crew comprised 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmarese nationals, and one Bangladeshi national [c30].

An Indian Navy P8I surveillance aircraft detected two floating liferafts near the reported position of M.V. Ocean Winner [c33]. The aircraft also spotted an oil slick in the area [c33]. Commercial vessel MT Aisopos rescued two Chinese crew members from liferafts by late evening on August 22, 2026 [c34]. Union Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that two survivors were rescued [c38]. Sonowal said the rescued crew received medical care [c38].

The search operation for the missing crew members continues [c44, c45]. The Indian Coast Guard deployed vessels ICGS Varad, ICGS Anmol, and ICGS Vijit to assist in search operations [c44]. Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal reported that rough sea conditions were slowing work [c45]. Uniyal said rough sea conditions in the Bay of Bengal were hampering search operations [c45].

Database records from Equasis show M.V. Ocean Winner was a 28-year-old vessel built in 1998 [c35]. The vessel measured 225 metres long and 32.26 metres wide [c35]. It had a capacity of around 73,000 tonnes [c35]. M.V. Ocean Winner's current owner is based in Fujian, China [c37]. Protection and Indemnity insurance covered the vessel starting August 1, 2026 [c37]. An inspection in Chittagong, Bangladesh, in June reported three deficiencies [c36]. One deficiency involved its magnetic compass [c36].

Similar maritime incidents have happened in Indian waters before [c46, c47]. In September 2009, the Mongolian-flagged bulk carrier MV Black Rose sank near Paradip [c46]. That vessel sank after developing a hull leak while carrying 23,847 tonnes of iron ore [c46]. In 2009, the MV Asian Forest capsized off Mangalore Port on India's west coast [c47]. That ship capsized due to cargo liquefaction after loading iron ore fines [c47].
